mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or UNRATE rise does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 2% year-over-year signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or INDPRO YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising CPIAUCSL (above 2% YoY) and falling FEDFUNDS (below 2%) signals a mismatch between inflation and monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or the interaction between CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS does not correlate with subsequent market performance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% year-over-year signals weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or HOUST decline does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a rising Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) and a falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong and balanced economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or the interaction between INDPRO and UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent market performance.
